title: Deep unsupervised learning for fishing activity recognition from automatic identification system data
content:
Abstract
Monitoring fishing behavior is crucial for marine conservation and ecosystem protection. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is a cost-effective tool for tracking vessel activity, yet traditional supervised learning models rely heavily on human-labeled data, limiting their ability to utilize vast amounts of unlabeled AIS records. To address this, we developed a deep learning architecture that progressively uses AIS data in a latent space. The model achieves >91% accuracy in a fully unsupervised setting and exceeds 92% accuracy with only 10% labeled data. Additional labels provide only marginal improvements, highlighting the strong discriminative power and label efficiency of the learned representations. Leveraging the high-precision fishing time inferred by this model, we demonstrate two key downstream applications. First, by integrating the fishing time with species distribution data, we enable a more accurate estimation of localized fishing pressure. Second, adopting a fishing ground forecasting framework, we independently modeled species catch data and fleet fishing time to compare their responses to environmental factors. This comparative analysis explicitly reveals the spatial mismatch and divergent environmental preferences between target species habitats and actual fishing operations. Overall, this study enhances fishing behavior detection and provides a robust foundation for data-driven, sustainable fisheries management.
